The email was sent with a subject line beginning exactly with \[CSE 3311 submission\]

The main highlight of Iteration 3 is the newly supported indoor navigation feature of a majority of buildings on campus. Almost all buildings now have an indoor navigation system support for them. Iteration 3 also brings two features planned during the Inception phase, those being high foot traffic avoidance and MyMav schedule importer. It is still a mobile website built using Expo \[1\], React Native \[2\], and React Native for Web \[3\], and everything still runs on the phone with no server or backend. The project is still hosted on GitHub Pages. This deliverable covers the planning and design without digging too much into the technical aspects. For more information on that, refer to the project’s [README.md](https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7/blob/main/README.md).

## Changes Since Iteration 2

### Indoor Mapping Done with Script, then Manually Edited

During this iteration, we determined that the work effort to manually map every single building on campus exceeds the reasonable amount of effort and time expected for this project, so with the help of Claude \[24\], we wrote an auto-trace script (Python, using PyMuPDF \[30\], RapidOCR \[31\], scikit-image \[32\], Shapely \[33\], and SciPy \[34\]). It read every building’s emergency exit diagram \[15\], which were vector drawings and drafted the indoor map for rooms, doors, hallways, stairs, and elevators. After several iterations of the script, we settled for a one that meets our standards and distributed the manual review of every auto traced building among all 4 group members.

### Door Rules

During a scouting of Nedderman Hall conducted a day after Iteration 2’s submission, Anthony discovered an issue that our indoor mapping did not account for. The existence of one-way and staff only doors. Routes would pass right through them and treat them as if they were not there. Anyone that chose to follow the route would either be stuck or set off an emergency alarm. This iteration brings Door Rules, allowing us to select and control the “flow of traffic” for doors and allow who goes in and who goes out from which direction for every door.

### Buildings Connected to Other Buildings

Iteration 2 also struggled to demonstrate that some buildings connect to other buildings, like Science Hall and the Chemistry Research Building. Iteration 3 brings the ability to add an entrance to a building that is not explicitly only for outdoor routing. Buildings now support entrances that connect to other buildings.

### Lazy Loading of Buildings

Iteration 2 only had two buildings fully mapped, those being Nedderman Hall and the Engineering Research Building. This meant that the overall size of the app was relatively small. With the introduction of over 50 newly traced buildings, the download size of the app has skyrocketed. Because of this, we introduced lazy loading to the indoor maps. This means that the indoors of buildings are only loaded whenever they are actually needed rather than when the app starts up, thus saving a lot of load time.

## Competitor Uniqueness

Iteration 3 places Mavigator above all other competitor’s tools in terms of uniqueness for navigating UTA specifically. 

| Feature / Capability | Google Maps \[26\] | UTA Static PDF  \[16\] | Modii (PATS Portal) \[27\] | UTA Interactive Map \[28\] | Maze Map \[29\] | Mavigator |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Outdoor Pedestrian Paths | Yes | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Permit-Filtered Parking | No | No | Partial | No | No | Yes |
| Personal Schedule Integration | No | No | No | No | Some | Yes |
| Indoor Room Navigation | No | No | No | No | Partial | Yes |
| Knows which doors are allowed to be used | No | No | No | No | Partial | Yes |
| Avoids known busy areas | No | No | No | No | Partial | Yes |
| Free | Yes | Yes | Needs login | Yes | Varies | Yes |

**How Mavigator differs:** it is the only tool that covers all the capabilities defined above. Three new ones have been added since Iteration 2, those being “Knows which doors are allowed to be used”, implemented via Door Rules, “Avoids known busy areas”, implemented via high foot traffic avoidance, and “Free”. It’s always been free but we just forgot to include it. Competitors are still ahead in terms of lot occupancy with Modii, which UTA doesn’t list publicly for us, Google Maps covering everything off campus, which is not in the scope of our goals, and our busy areas are not live crowd monitoring, as specified during the Inception phase.

# Risk Evaluation

This iteration retired one risk before it made it into an official written deliverable submission. It also came with 2 new risks that made it into our top 5 risks.

## Retired Risks

| Risk | Was | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R-15 (new): Load time grows with every mapped building. | 2.0 | Retired in the same iteration it was created. With 50 buildings being downloaded when the site loads, the load time grew greatly. We ended up switching to a lazy loading method where we only loaded buildings that were required for routing to cut down on load time. |

## Risks

| ID | Risk | Category | Probability | Impact | Exposure | Change |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R-12 (new) | Auto traced indoor maps have many errors and missed rooms, stairs, etc. | Data quality | 50% | 20 | 10 | New |
| R-04 | Some rooms or floors cannot be mapped | External data | 70% | 3 | 2.1 | Realized for ERB floor 6 and handled |
| R-10 | Floor plan source is copyrighted (UTA EHS evacuation diagrams \[15\]) | Legal | 40% | 5 | 2.0 | Same as before, now for 50 buildings |
| R-13 (new) | MyMav pages differ in copy paste format from what the parser was tuned to. | External format | 30% | 4 | 1.2 | New |
| R-08 | No indoor plans for remaining buildings | External data | 5% | 20 | 1.0 | Down from 4.0. Diagrams were found for every building we mapped. |

## Risk Mitigation Plans

* R-12: Auto trace errors are found on basically every building that was auto traced. We took all 48 auto traced buildings and distributed the manual review effort of these buildings among every member. This covered a majority of the work done in iteration 3\. We fixed things like missing room data, missing stairwells and elevators, replacing rooms that were supposed to be restrooms with restrooms, and made the auto traced results look less jagged and spikey.  
* R-04: A floor can be marked as “can’t be mapped” so the app will say so instead of drawing an empty floor. ERB floor 6 is still not fixed but will be in Iteration 4\.  
* R-10: The diagrams are never on the repo, and we made sure of this. The auto trace script never saves the PDF. Our permission request to UTA EHS has not been sent yet. If UTA says no, the fallback is to put indoor maps behind a UTA only login.  
* R-13: MyMav shows the results of different class lists in a different format for some browsers. The risk comes from not being able to cover all of them with the parser. However with enough data, we can safely say that our parser covers a majority of formats.  
* R-08: Only a building with no diagram at all causes this risk. The general academic building is a good example because it only has a diagram for the bottom left building. We can go into the building and manually map it out.

# Design

All data is generated at build time and all routing runs on the phone, so the app needs no server. This section follows a simplified IEEE 1016 \[20\].

## Architecture

Iteration 2 feedback said that drawing many components in one box hides how they work together, so following the feedback, we have these structures. The preview looked so incredibly bad if we pasted it into this document that it was committed to the repo and can be [found here](https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7/blob/main/developer_documents/iteration_3_documents/system_architecture.md). It’s a structure map of the app components at run time.

| Element | Responsibility | Key properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Screens | Show the map, schedule, parking and settings, take touches | React Native components, never compute routes themselves |
| Route screen / Indoor route screen | Draw one route, outdoor leg on the campus map, indoor leg floor by floor | Shared by the Map and Schedule tabs, so a fix lands in both |
| ScheduleProvider | Holds the class list and the app's clock | The clock drives class status, parking rules and busy areas |
| Stores (src/state) | Permit, start point, theme, units, time format, Avoid crowds | Module-level, shared by every screen, saved through KeyValueStorage |
| KeyValueStorage (new) | Interface for reading and writing saved values by key. browserStorage wraps localStorage, memoryStorage() is for tests | Hides which storage is used: tests no longer fake a browser global, and a phone-app storage can be added without changing the code that saves |
| usePlaceRoute | The only caller of the router. Turns "this building and room" into a route, its two legs and its crowd report | Waits for the destination's indoor map to load, then recomputes when the start, the clock, or Avoid crowds changes |
| start-point | Resolves the chosen start (GPS, pin, residence, lot, room) to a place | Stored as a reference, so a map re-import can't move it |
| graph / campus-graph | Builds the outdoor graph at startup and adds each building's indoor graph when it is first needed (useCampusGraph) | Directed: a door's rule can block one direction. Staff-only steps are marked restricted. A building loads once and stays |
| route | Snaps both ends to the graph, ends at the best entrance or the room's door | Never snaps GPS onto an indoor node |
| dijkstra | Shortest path with a binary min-heap | Orders by cost (room and crowd penalties) but reports real meters |
| foot-traffic | Finds which walkways are in a busy area now, and makes them cost more | Busy areas are known peak times, not live data |
| legs | Splits a route where it enters the building | Outdoor leg (walk or bike), indoor leg (walk) |
| directions | Turns a path into steps ("Take the stairs up to floor 3") | Simplifies the line first (Douglas-Peucker \[18\]) |
| parking-recommendation | Ranks lots the permit allows by walking time to the class | One shortest-path tree from the class, not one search per lot |
| mymav-parser | Reads a pasted MyMav page into classes | Pure, lists every meeting it can't place, with why |

Every input the user or the phone gives the app, and what the app shows in return. Only items that are new or changed are included, the rest remain the same. 

| Feature | Inputs | Outputs |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Building preview (changed) | 1: Outside / Inside toggle (now any of 50 mapped buildings) \| 2: floor picker \| 3: tap a room \| 4: Set as destination / Set Room \_\_\_ as destination | 1: name, category, abbreviation, outline, the building's indoor map starts downloading \| 2: that floor's rooms, stairs, elevators, restrooms ("Loading the indoor map…" until it arrives) \| 3: room highlighted \| 4: route screen |
| Route screen (outdoor) | 1: destination \| 2: start point \| 3: Walk / Bike \| 4: open the drawer \| 5: Go inside \| 6: back chip | 1: route line to the best public entrance \| 2: distance and ETA \| 3: outdoor ETA changes \| 4: steps \| 5: indoor screen \| 6: previous screen |
| Avoid crowds (new) | 1: Avoid crowds chip on / off \| 2: the app's clock and weekday | 1: route goes around busy areas, or walks through when there is no way round \| 2: busy areas drawn in amber only during their peak times \| a note: "Going around the Central Library (busy now), \+2 min", "No way around…", "Passes…, busy now", "This walk stays clear" or "No busy areas right now" |
| Door rules (new) | Destination room behind a staff-only or one-way door | Route avoids doors that can't be used that way \| "Room N is in a staff-only area, so there's no public way in." if none can \| gate bars drawn across hallways (red closed, amber staff, blue one way) |
| MyMav import (new) | 1: pasted text of the MyMav schedule page (week view or List View) \| 2: Read schedule \| 3: Add N classes | 1: (after 2\) a card per class: code, name, building, room, days, times, "already on your schedule" for repeats \| "Not imported" list with reasons \| "No classes found…" if nothing matched \| 3: classes added, "Schedule imported: Added N classes", back to the schedule |
| Saving (web) (changed) | Any change to schedule, permit, theme, start point, units, time format or Avoid crowds \| reload | Saved to localStorage, restored after reload \| corrupt data ignored |
| Developer (temporary) | Clock offset \| test class \| start inside NH | Simulated time (also moves busy areas) \| test class \| route starts at a room door |

## Route Calculation

Some parts of the route calculation have changed since Iteration 2\.

1. Every tab asks one hook, usePlaceRoute(target, from), for a route.  
2. (new) The hook loads the destination building's indoor map if it isn't loaded yet (and the start building's, for a start inside a room). Until it arrives, the route screens say "Loading the indoor map".  
3. The hook resolves the start point to a coordinate or node.  
4. findRoute snaps the start to the walkway graph and ends at the building's nearest public entrance, or at the room's door.  
5. (changed) shortestPath (Dijkstra \[17\]) runs on a directed graph. A door with a rule is one or two one-way steps: a "no one" step is left out, and a "staff" step is skipped. When Avoid crowds is on and a busy area is active, each outdoor walkway inside it costs 4 times its length, so a 50 m crowd is worth a 150 m detour. Room edges still cost an extra 1,000 m. Reported distances are always real meters.  
6. (new) If no public path exists but one through staff-only doors does, the route screen says the room is in a staff-only area. When avoiding crowds, the hook also runs the search without the crowd cost to report what was avoided and how many minutes it adds.  
7. splitRoute cuts the route where it enters the building.  
8. routeDirections writes the steps, now including "Go into Chemistry and Physics Building" for a door between buildings.

Parking uses one shortestPathTree from the class building instead of one search per lot.

## Use Cases for Iteration 3 Features

UC-01: Select Parking Permit and Find Parking for the Next Class  
Actor: student  
Main flow:

1. The student opens the Parking tab.  
2. They tap the pass chip and pick their permit. Every lot is recolored for that permit at the app's time.  
3. They open the drawer. The app takes their next class today and ranks the lots the permit allows by walking time to that class's building, at the class start time.  
4. They tap a lot. The walking route from it to the class is drawn.

Exceptional flows:

* No permit chosen ("None"): every lot is red, and the drawer asks for a permit.  
* No class left today: the drawer says so instead of ranking lots.  
* The class's building is not on the map: the drawer says so.  
* A lot with no permit rule: drawn gray, never shown as "not allowed".  
* After 7 PM and on weekends: every known lot is allowed.

UC-04: Toggle Traffic Avoidance  
Actor: student  
Precondition: a route screen is open with a start point and a destination.  
Main flow:

1. The app checks the app's clock against the known busy areas.  
2. Busy areas active now are drawn in amber on the map.  
3. The student taps Avoid crowds.  
4. The app recomputes the route with crowded walkways made costlier and draws the new route.  
5. The note says which busy areas the route goes around and how many minutes that adds ("Going around the Central Library (busy now), \+2 min").  
6. Tapping the chip again returns the direct route. The choice is saved for next time.

Exceptional flows:

* 3a. No busy area active now: the note says "No busy areas right now." and the route does not change.  
* 4a. No way around (the destination is inside the busy area, or the detour costs more): the route still walks through, and the note says "No way around the University Center, busy now."  
* 4b. Avoid crowds off but the route passes a busy area: the note warns "Passes the Central Library, busy now."  
* 4c. Busy areas active, but the direct route doesn't pass them: "Busy now: the Central Library. This walk stays clear."  
* 5a. Biking: the added time uses biking speed.

US-05: Import Schedule from MyMav  
Actor: student  
Precondition: the student can open MyMav.  
Main flow:

1. The student opens Settings \> Your Profile \> Schedule \> Import from MyMav.  
2. Following the on-screen instructions, they copy their whole MyMav schedule page (the week view, or the List View of My Class Schedule) and paste it.  
3. They tap Read schedule.  
4. The app shows one card per class: course, building and room, days and times. In the week view, a course that meets on Tuesday and Thursday becomes one class meeting on both days.  
5. They tap Add N classes. The classes are added to the schedule in time order, the app says "Added N classes", and returns to the schedule.

Exceptional flows:

* 4a. Nothing recognized: "No classes found. Copy the whole schedule page and try again."  
* 4b. A meeting can't be placed (online, TBA, or a building not on the map): it is listed under Not imported with the reason, never dropped silently. The student can add it by hand.  
* 4c. A class is already on the schedule: its card says "already on your schedule", and it is not counted or added again. If every class is a repeat, there is no Add button.  
* 4d. The student edits the pasted text: the preview clears until they tap Read schedule again.  
* 4e. The week view lists no end time: the end time is guessed (80 minutes for Tuesday/Thursday, 50 otherwise) and shown on the card, the on-screen instructions ask the student to check it.  
* 4f. A class is dropped or waitlisted: listed under Not imported ("Status is Dropped, not enrolled.").

UC-05 extension: Route to a room behind a restricted door  
Main flow as in Iteration 2 (route to a room's door).   
Exceptional flows added:

* Only a staff-only door leads to the room: both route screens show "Room N is in a staff-only area, so there's no public way in." and no route.  
* A one-way door is on the shortest path the wrong way: the route takes the next-best path through doors that open that way. Gate bars on the indoor map show why.  
* The room is in a connected building: the route crosses through the connecting door, and directions say "Go into ".

## Handled Exceptional Cases

Only lists what’s new in Iteration 3, the old list still applies.

* A room reachable only through a staff-only door: message, no route.  
* One-way and alarmed doors: never used the wrong way, and never offered as a way in.  
* Avoid crowds with no busy area, no way around, or a route that already stays clear: the note says which.  
* A crowd zone moved off every walkway (onto a roof or off campus): a data test fails.  
* MyMav paste with nothing recognized, with online/TBA/unknown-building meetings, with classes already on the schedule, with no end times (week view), or with dropped or waitlisted classes.  
* A building's indoor map still downloading: the route screens and the building preview say "Loading the indoor map" instead of drawing a route to the door and then jumping to the room. If the download fails (offline), it is tried again the next time the screen opens, the add-class room check skips the room check rather than blocking.  
* A floor split into pieces by a tracing gap: the data test fails on any split not listed as known, so the bug behind Tan's feedback can't come back unnoticed.  
* A room door that no entrance reaches: the data test fails and the import report names it.

# Code

Over 200,000 lines were added this iteration alone. While this may seem like an absurd amount (it is), most added lines are generated map and indoor data from our Campus Digitizer and were JSON files needed for the generation of many indoor mapped buildings. The table below only lists the changes to the code made in Iteration 3\.

| Module | Path | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Foot traffic | src/routing/foot-traffic.ts, src/constants/foot-traffic.ts, src/state/avoid-crowds.ts | Busy areas, their peak times, the crowd cost and the route note |
| MyMav import | src/context/mymav-parser.ts, src/app/settings/profile/import.tsx | Parse a pasted schedule, preview and add |
| Door Rules | tools/indoor/indoor.ts, src/routing/graph.ts, src/routing/dijkstra.ts | Import door rules into one-way and staff-only edges, skip them when routing |
| Indoor reviews | indoor-reviews/, npm run merge:reviews | One reviewed file per building, merged into indoor-edits.json |
| Saved settings | src/state/key-value-storage.ts, persist.ts, schedule-context.tsx | Saving goes through the KeyValueStorage interface instead of localStorage directly |
| Route screens | src/components/routing/ | Avoid crowds chip, staff-only message, gate bars |
| Indoor data | src/data/indoor-edits.json, src/data/indoor/ (one file per building), campus-indoor.ts (the index) | 50 buildings, each its own download |
| Loading indoor maps | src/routing/campus-graph.ts, src/hooks/use-place-route.ts, tools/osm/import.mts | useCampusGraph loads a building on first use and adds it to the graph, the import writes one file per building |

## Notable Code

* Crowd cost, not crowd blocking. A crowded walkway costs 4 times its length instead of being removed, so a route goes around only when going around is cheaper, and still reaches a destination inside the busy area. Distances and ETAs shown are the real meters walked.  
* Reporting the detour. With Avoid crowds on, the hook runs a second search without the crowd cost and compares the two, which is how the note knows what was avoided and how many minutes it adds.  
* Directed graph for door rules. Every edge was usable both ways until Iteration 3\. Now a door's rule can drop one direction ("no one") or mark it restricted ("staff"). Public entrances are the only ones routes may end at, but exit-only doors can still be used to leave.  
* The parser never drops data. Every meeting it can't place is returned with a reason, so the user always sees what was not imported.  
* Indoor maps on demand. The import writes each building's indoor data to its own module, and the index loads it with import(), which the web build turns into a separate file. The graph is held in a small store: it starts with the outdoor walkways and is rebuilt (a few milliseconds) each time a building arrives, and every screen reading it re-renders.  
* One file per reviewed building. Four people reviewing at once never edit the same file, so there were no merge conflicts in the indoor data.

## Static Analysis

Aside from the normal project’s test, we ran ESLint \[37\] with typescript-eslint’s strict type-checked rules \[38\]. It reported 494 problems over 16 rules. We looked at the riskiest ones and determined if any of them are legitimate. Most were determined to not be an issue. Iteration 4 may make fixes to these.

## Unit Tests

All 560 Jest \[9\] tests in 41 files pass, up from 506 tests in 36 files at Iteration 2\. All of these tests were written by AI (Claude \[24\]) asked to obtain significant coverage over the file they were testing. TypeScript \[8\] type check and lint report 0 problems. Test documentation follows a simplified ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 \[21\].

| Area | New or changed tests in Iteration 3 |
| :---- | :---- |
| Foot traffic (src/routing/\_\_tests\_\_/foot-traffic.test.ts) | Which zones are active by day and time, which walkways a zone's box covers, the crowd cost, the route note for each case |
| Dijkstra and campus routes | Custom edge cost, on the real campus, a route goes around the library at noon on a weekday for a couple of extra minutes |
| MyMav parser | List view, phone layout (one field per line, MWF/TR days), the week view from a real paste (one class across the days it meets, guessed end times, dropped classes skipped), meetings it can't place and why, a meeting listed twice, text that isn't a schedule |
| Indoor builder | Door rules on every door kind, hallway gates, entrances into another building |
| Saved settings (src/state/\_\_tests\_\_/persist.test.ts) | Uses memoryStorage() instead of faking the browser's localStorage, new case: no storage available |
| Campus data | Every room door reachable, no unknown split floors, every crowd zone covers a walkway, indoor buildings found by abbreviation or id. These tests load every building's file at once (loadAllIndoor) |

# How To Test / Run

If you want to simply see the website itself, it is now hosted at [antovu.github.io/cse3311-fall26-group7](https://antovu.github.io/cse3311-fall26-group7/map), though we may choose to move away from GitHub Pages at a certain point for a better URL. As for running the code itself:

`git clone https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7.git`  
`cd cse3311-fall26-group7`  
`npm install`  
`npx expo start --web --tunnel`  
`npm test      #in a different terminal if tunnel still running`

Please note: this project is designed as a website now, but is still made specifically to be used on the phone. Future iterations may improve the looks and functionality on desktop, but for now, desktop testing should not be a priority. The site was also checked at phone size in an emulated touch browser using Playwright \[10\]. Navigate to the link provided by the tunnel to test on your phone.  
Test the additions of Iteration 3, those being the indoor mapping of every building, avoid crowds (using developer settings if you need) and MyMav import. Copy and paste your schedule from the List view only MyMav under Manage Classes. This process will be better explained in iteration 4\.
